verdict.rationale: Lithic documents its own card-level scoping controls: virtual card creation, Authorization Rules applied to specific cards using attributes like MCC, country and currency, and card spend limits. That covers 'tightly scoped' cards in part. Nothing in the pack documents a single-use card type, locking a card to one specific merchant, or an exact-amount authorization limit. ASA custom approval logic is only a developer building block and earns no credit. Missing for 10: documented single-use card type, merchant-locked cards, exact-amount authorization, auto-invalidation after first use, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can issue single-use and tightly scoped cards — one purchase, one merchant, an exact amount — so a leaked number is worthless the moment it's used

citations.quote: Create a new virtual or physical card.
By defining rules based on high-signal attributes like MCC, country, currency, and risk score, you can enforce business-specific authorization logic at the program, account, or card level
